answer: Randomly re-drawn grading juries per round convert reputation into a repeated, sampling-based test: each identity’s observed score is validated by a fresh panel, so a Sybil cluster cannot amortize one favorable juror set across many pseudonyms. The attacker’s marginal cost per fake identity therefore rises with the probability of adverse review in every round, since a single dissenting vertex in the jury graph can void the payoff. Reputation thus behaves less like a fable of permanent standing and more like an oasis that must be re-earned; forgery scales linearly in identities while.
